title: Architecture work
description: The files the architecture team of one Epic hands to each other and to the script: the solutions architect's state, its requests to the specialists and their answers with their digest, its result, the lead's routing, the question put to the decider and its ruling, and the comparison of what a Story built. The root is the architect's result; each other file has its own schema file that refers to its definition here. A matrix id is the id of an entry as atw-matrix prints it.

NeedState.description: The architect's first judgment of one need against the effective architecture (arc42 and detailed, as it stands before this Epic). Effective means approved, never complete or correct; it iterates with each Epic (effective-architecture skill, "Lifecycle, the baseline and iteration"). `approved`: the architect judges that effective statements meet the need as they stand. `disagreement`: effective statements bear on the need and two of them disagree. `missing`: no effective statement meets the need.

StateConclusion.description: The architect's first judgment, a starting point and no result. `effective-architecture-meets-every-need`: every need is `approved`, so the architect's work starts from the questions its expertise raises about the effective architecture. `work-remains`: at least one need is `disagreement` or `missing`.

Conclusion.description: What the architect concluded. Every conclusion goes through the architecture check; the architect reviews and approves its own architecture against the criteria, and nothing else reviews it. `no-change-needed`: the architect judged that the Epic needs nothing added, changed or removed in the approved architecture, and `criteria` cites the effective documents and headings that meet it. `changes-designed`: the architect designed, changed, removed or settled something for the Epic. `unsettled`: at least one matter is listed in `unsettled`.

CriterionStatus.description: `satisfied`: `satisfiedAt` names where. `not-applicable`: `reason` says why the criterion does not apply to this PRD.

UnsettledKind.description: `technical-choice`: two positions remain, each with evidence and a real cost. `business-conflict`: two business requirements that no design meets together, or a design that only works against section 2.

RequestKind.description: `question`: one question to answer. `task`: one bounded piece of design, or one diagram to draw.

TrdMode.description: `complete`: the one TRD write after the solutions architect's decisions, once the architecture check passes: the TRD at `trdPath` is the seed the script `trd.seed` wrote from the constraints that bind the Epic; add the requirements not considered functional (the quality constraints and operational boundaries the technical architecture must support) that the PRD implies and the TRD does not state, apply the listed changes, and write each listed shared capability the TRD does not yet state. `update`: apply the listed changes and nothing else; the correction the TRD confirm step asks for is one.

RequirementKind.description: `obligation`: something that must be true of an element, with a checkable value. `reuse`: the element obtains a behaviour from a shared capability and does not implement its own.

Routing.description: What the lead decides for one item. `reject`: the matter goes no further. `correct`: the architect corrects it. `opinion`: one specialist is asked, and the answer goes to the architect with the correction. `competing-design`: the architect designs the other position of one matter. `decider`: the decider rules.

OwnerConcernKind.description: `business-conflict`: two business requirements cannot both be met by any design. `section-2-conflict`: the only workable design conflicts with a section 2 constraint.

SourceHeading.description: Where something is stated or can be checked.

source.description: An architecture document's path relative to the architecture root, a PRD or TRD path, an AWS documentation URL, code as repository, revision and file:line, or an earlier specialist's answer file.

heading.description: The heading in that document, or the id of the PRD or TRD requirement; an empty string when the source has none.

Need.description: One thing the PRD needs of the architecture, and the architect's judgment of it.

id.description: N1, N2 and so on, unique in the file.

need.description: What the PRD needs, in one sentence.

prdRequirements.description: The PRD requirement headings the need comes from.

evidence.description: The approved statements judged, and for a disagreement the statements that disagree.

judgment.description: Why the state is what it is.

ArchitectureContext.description: The context file of one Epic's architecture work. The open-run step of the elaboration writes it; every step of the architecture part is handed it, and the solutions architect's brief names it as `context`. It names every path the script chose, so that no agent and no step derives one.

architectureRoot.description: The architecture folder of the vault, which holds `arc42/`, `detailed/`, `built/` and `reference/`.

vaultCommit.description: The vault commit the matrix's document rows are synced to.

matrixCommand.description: The command that reads and writes the matrix.

statePath.description: Where the solutions architect writes its state file.

resultPath.description: Where the solutions architect writes its result file.

reviewLogPath.description: Where the solutions architect writes the Epic's review log, beside its result, to the log-architecture-review skill's `review-log.schema.json`. Consumed by: the check step (orchestrator/flows/architecture_check.py), which fails the result on a log that is missing, malformed, has a decision without its options and reason, or leaves an AWS resource of the design without a review entry; and the promotion step (orchestrator/flows/architecture_promotion.py), which commits the log with the Epic's architecture in the vault and links it from the Epic's matrix entry.

trdPath.description: Where the TRD of this Epic is written and kept; every TRD request names this path.

helpersFolder.description: The folder for the request files the solutions architect writes and the answer files it names in them.

CheckResult.description: What the check step of the architecture part found before promotion: every defect a script can find in the matrix, in the documents it indexes, in the solutions architect's result and in its review log. The script writes it; when `valid` is false the solutions architect is handed it as `findings` and corrects each problem.

valid.description: True when the check found no problem.

unansweredCriteria.description: The ids of the architecture and technical-requirement criteria the result gives no answer for.

corrections.description: How many corrections of mechanical defects came before this check.

ArchitectureState.description: The solutions architect's judgment of the state of the architecture for this PRD, written before it does anything else.

FeatureEntry.description: One feature the PRD needs, as the architect recorded it in the matrix.

id.description: The matrix id of the feature entry.

prdRequirements.description: The PRD requirement headings the feature serves.

elements.description: The matrix ids of the elements that realize it.

sharedCapabilities.description: The matrix ids of the supporting features it uses.

NoFeature.description: One PRD requirement the architect judges no feature serves, with the reason.

requirement.description: The matrix id of the requirement, or its PRD requirement heading.

reason.description: Why no feature serves it: for example, it states no behaviour of the system.

ReachVerdictKind.description: `kept`: the link that puts the entry in reach is true for this PRD and the entry is used as the pack lists it. `corrected`: it stays in reach and the architect corrected the entry or the link. `pruned`: the link over-reached and the architect removed it, so the entry is no longer in the Epic's reach.

ReachVerdict.description: The architect's verdict on one entry of the Epic's reach: a row of the architecture pack's `reach`, or an entry the architect's corrections brought into the reach.

id.description: The entry's matrix id, as the pack lists it.

via.description: The links that put the entry in reach, as the pack lists them; for an entry the corrections brought in, the link that does.

Exclusion.description: One reached service, component, piece of infrastructure or layer that no stack builds, with the reason.

reason.description: Why no stack builds it: for example, it is a third-party service the Epic only calls.

SharedUse.description: One element that obtains behaviours from a shared capability and does not implement them itself, by pointer: `atw-matrix node <capability>` returns each `provides` item with its `behaviour`, `consumersMust`, `interface`, `useSignals` and `duplicateSignals`.

element.description: The matrix id of the element that uses the capability.

capability.description: The matrix id of the supporting feature.

relies.description: The ids of the capability's `provides` items the element obtains, as the `supportedBy` relationship's `relies` records them.

FactEntry.description: One design fact with its one home.

id.description: The id of the fact, unique in the file.

statement.description: The fact, in the form its home document requires: an arc42 section's form, or the detailed design of one component, one feature, components working together or the whole system.

home.description: The one architecture document and heading that states the fact: a document under `arc42/`, or under `detailed/` for detail the architecture documentation model places there.

linkedFrom.description: The paths, relative to the architecture root, of the documents that link to the home and do not restate the fact.

about.description: The matrix ids of the entries the fact is about; empty for a fact about none. Consumed by: the step of orchestrator/flows/architecture.py that accepts the document write of the fact's home, which records `describedBy` from each entry to the home heading, and `covers` from that heading to each requirement an entry among them serves as a feature. The output check of the architect's result refuses an id the matrix, with the change file applied, does not hold.

CriterionAnswer.description: The architect's answer to one criterion of effective-architecture/review-criteria.json whose level is architecture or technical-requirement.

satisfiedAt.description: For `satisfied`, each architecture document and heading, or the TRD path with a requirement id as the heading, that satisfies it; empty for `not-applicable`.

reason.description: For `not-applicable`, why the criterion does not apply to this PRD; an empty string for `satisfied`.

Position.description: One of the positions on a matter.

id.description: A short name for the position, unique in the matter.

UnsettledMatter.description: A matter the architect could not settle, or the question the lead puts to the decider: the matter and the positions on it.

id.description: U1, U2 and so on, unique in the file.

matter.description: What has to be decided, in one or two sentences.

CostEvidence.description: The unit math behind one cost constraint in the TRD.

resource.description: The matrix id of the billable element.

assumptions.description: The stated usage the estimate rests on.

unitMath.description: The arithmetic, with the fixed monthly floor kept apart from usage cost.

RecommendationAction.description: `create`: a specialist no agent is. `update`: an existing agent.

SpecialistRecommendation.description: One recommendation to the owner to create a specialist agent or to update one, from a subject the solutions architect designed with its own tools and resources because no specialist covered it, or covered it without what the subject needed. Consumed by: the architect step of orchestrator/flows/architecture.py, which records it in the step journal; orchestrator/flows/elaboration_result.py adds it to the elaboration handback's `requiredHumanActions`, which the driver records in the owner's human-action log. The design of the subject is in the architecture, never left to the recommendation.

agent.description: The existing agent's name for `update`; the proposed name for `create`.

subject.description: The subject of this Epic's design the architect designed itself.

recommendation.description: What the specialist would cover or hold (instructions, skills, tools) so that it serves the subject next time.

SpecialistRequest.description: What the solutions architect, or the lead when it asks for an opinion, asks of one agent: a question or a bounded piece of design. The script starts the agent with it as its own session; no agent starts another.

bounds.description: For a task, exactly what is to be decided and what is not; an empty string for a question.

concerns.description: The PRD sections and architecture headings the request concerns, and nothing wider.

trustedCode.description: The matrix ids of the entries the matrix marks verified. Code of any other entry is a hint only.

answerPath.description: The absolute path the answer is written to, under the context file's `helpersFolder`.

AgentRequest.description: One request to one agent, with the agent the architect chose for it: the agent's whole share of one round, its questions and draft reviews together.

agent.description: The name of the agent that does the work, as the find-specialists skill's catalog lists it. The script refuses a name the catalog does not list.

SpecialistRound.description: The first round of requests to the specialists, written by the solutions architect's Analyze step at `questions.json` beside the context file. Consumed by: the step of orchestrator/flows/architecture.py that accepts it, which refuses an agent the find-specialists catalog does not list and two requests to one agent, writes each request beside its answer path and plans one step per request whose answer is not yet a valid answer, then the architect's Decide step, handed every answer and a digest of them.

requests.description: One request per agent; empty when the Epic needs no specialist.

Restatement.description: A place that states a fact a second time, to be replaced by a link to the fact's home.

fact.description: The id of the fact in this request, or a short name for a fact an effective document states.

AppliedSettlement.description: A settled disagreement to apply to the documents.

disagreement.description: The matrix id of the disagreement entry.

corrections.description: Each place whose statement lost and is replaced by a link to the one that stands.

Diagram.description: One diagram for architecture-maintainer to place.

home.description: The architecture document (under `arc42/` or `detailed/`) and heading the diagram belongs under.

viewType.description: The view type, from the documentation model's list of view types.

mermaid.description: The Mermaid source, without the code fence.

shows.description: The names of the elements the diagram shows.

TrdChange.description: One change to the TRD. For `remove`, only `id` carries meaning and the other texts are empty.

id.description: The requirement id; for `add`, an empty string lets trd-author assign the next id; for a `change` the TRD confirm step states about the front matter or a citation, an empty string.

statement.description: What must be true, with its checkable value.

appliesTo.description: The matrix id of the element.

ArchitectureResult.description: The solutions architect's result for one Epic, at the context file's `resultPath`: its decisions. The architect's Decide step writes it as the work goes, so that a session that stops loses nothing: the members settled so far, rewritten in place each time a part settles (a fact and its home, a settlement, a feature, a criterion answer). Every later architect step (a second Decide, a correction, a competing design) is a fresh session that continues from this file. The script reads `conclusion`, starts the agent each entry of `requests` names with its request, writes the documents from `facts`, `restatements`, `settlements` and `diagrams`, and checks every criterion answer and the review log at the context file's `reviewLogPath`; what is unapproved comes from the matrix, not from this file. The architect reviews and approves its own architecture against the criteria; the promotion step then sets it effective.

noFeature.description: Every requirement of the Epic that no feature serves. The step that accepts the result fails on a requirement that is neither served by a feature nor listed here.

addedOrChangedElements.description: The matrix ids, as recorded, of every element this design adds or changes for the Epic (services, components, infrastructure, events, routing rules, layers and packages), including every element a TRD requirement binds that this design adds or changes. The Epic's Stories build these and the elements of `unchangedWorkElements`, and nothing more. An element the Epic only uses is not listed: it is context for the Tasks, never work. An event is built in each stack that holds one of its producers. The step that accepts the result fails on an id the matrix lacks, an entry not on the architecture side, an event with no description, and an entry built in no stack (for an event, one none of whose producers is homed in a stack).

unchangedWorkElements.description: The matrix ids, as recorded, of the existing architecture-side elements (services, components, infrastructure, events, routing rules, layers and packages) that this design leaves unchanged and where the Epic has work, such as new wording on an existing page, as the architect names them from its design. An Epic can have both: a new service in `addedOrChangedElements` and new wording on an existing page here. Consumed by: the output check of orchestrator/flows/architecture.py, which fails when both lists are empty and on each problem `repo_scoping.story_build_problems` reports for these ids; and the span step of orchestrator/flows/repo_scoping.py, whose Stories build in these as well as in `addedOrChangedElements`.

sharedCapabilities.description: Every shared capability the design uses, as the `supportedBy` relationships the architect recorded state them.

facts.description: The design facts this run decided, each with its one home. Consumed by: the step of orchestrator/flows/architecture.py that accepts the result with no open request, which writes one write request per group of arc42 sections (1 to 5 with detailed/, 6 and 7, 8 to 12) from `facts`, `restatements`, `settlements` and `diagrams` and plans one architecture-maintainer step for each group whose request differs from the one already written.

restatements.description: Each place that restates a fact and is to be replaced by a link to its home; it goes to the write request of the group of the document it is in.

settlements.description: Each disagreement this run settled, with the statement that stands and each place whose statement lost; each place goes to the write request of its document's group.

diagrams.description: Each diagram to place: one a diagram author drew, as its answer file holds it, or one the architect drew; it goes to the write request of its home document's group.

criteria.description: One answer for every criterion whose level is architecture or technical-requirement. A criterion with neither a place it is satisfied nor a reason it does not apply is unfinished work.

specialistRecommendations.description: Each recommendation to the owner to create or update a specialist agent; empty when the specialists covered every subject.

trdChanges.description: Every technical or architecture decision of this design that adds, changes or removes a requirement of the TRD, as one change each; empty when the design changes none. The TRD the architect works from is the seed the script wrote from the constraints that bind the Epic, each requirement headed by its constraint id. Consumed by: the TRD write that the check step of orchestrator/flows/architecture_check.py plans before the promotion, whose request (`trd-request.schema.json`, mode `complete`) carries these changes and this result's `sharedCapabilities`.

requests.description: A second round of requests, one per agent, for what the answers the step was handed raise; empty when the decisions need none. Consumed by: the step of orchestrator/flows/architecture.py that accepts the result, which plans after that step one step for each request whose answer file is not yet a valid answer, started as the agent the entry names and handed its request, then a fresh Decide step, handed every answer and a digest of them; a Decide of the second round whose result still requests work fails, because the architecture does not converge. The script decides nothing about which agent runs.

reach.description: One verdict per entry of the Epic's reach: every row of the architecture pack's `reach`, and every entry the architect's corrections brought into the reach. Consumed by: the check step of orchestrator/flows/architecture_check.py, which recomputes the reach (`matrixtraverse.approval_scope`) on the matrix after the architect's change file is applied and fails each entry in it, other than the Epic and its requirements, with no `kept` or `corrected` verdict, and each `pruned` entry still in it; and the promotion step, which compares each `kept` entry with its `contentHash` before it approves.

excluded.description: Each reached service, component, piece of infrastructure or layer with no home stack that no stack builds, with the reason; empty when every one is placed. Consumed by: the check step of orchestrator/flows/architecture_check.py, which fails each such entry with no stack that is not listed here.

NeededSpecialty.description: Another specialty the answer needs, for the architect to ask.

DesignFact.description: One decision a bounded task returns, for the architect to accept or change.

belongsIn.description: Where the fact belongs, by the architecture documentation model: the arc42 section, 3 to 8, or the folder of the detailed architecture that holds it: `detailed/system`, `detailed/cross-component`, `detailed/components/<component>` or `detailed/features/<feature>`.

SpecialistAnswer.description: A design specialist's or diagram author's answer to one request.

kind.description: The request's `kind`, as the request file states it. An answer to a `question` has no `decisions` and no `diagrams`; an answer to a `task` has both.

answer.description: The answer to the question in one sentence, or for a task what was decided in one sentence.

assumptions.description: What the answer rests on that the sources do not establish.

alternatives.description: The alternatives considered; empty unless the request asks for them.

decisions.description: For a task, the decisions as design facts; absent for a question.

diagrams.description: For a diagram task, the diagrams drawn; empty for any other task; absent for a question.

DiagramSummary.description: What a diagram an answer holds shows, without its Mermaid source.

DigestedAnswer.description: One specialist answer, cut to what a decision needs: its reasons, alternatives and Mermaid sources stay in the answer file.

answerPath.description: The answer file, to read in full when a decision turns on its reasons.

decisions.description: A task's decisions; empty for a question.

diagrams.description: A task's diagrams, without their source; empty for a question.

AnswersDigest.description: The answers one architect step is handed, digested by the script that launches it (orchestrator/flows/architecture.py) into the helpers folder, so the architect reads a few KB instead of every answer file.

TrdRequest.description: What trd-author is asked. The script writes every request: the request of mode `complete` from the solutions architect's result (its `trdChanges` and `sharedCapabilities`) once the architecture check passes, and the request of mode `update` the TRD confirm step writes for what it found does not resolve. Its sources are not listed here: every session of trd-author is handed the Epic's architecture pack (`pack.json`, labelled `architecture pack`), an index that names the PRD, the Epic's requirements, the file of the constraints that apply with their statements and the headings they are stated in, and the heading references (`<path>#<heading>`) that describe what the Epic reaches, whose text `atw-matrix heading` prints.

epic.description: The Epic's beads id, which `atw-matrix epic` takes.

prdPath.description: The PRD file, which the architecture pack names; trd-author reads it, each requirement's `name` its PRD heading.

trdPath.description: The absolute path of the TRD file.

sharedCapabilities.description: For `complete`, every shared capability the design uses; trd-author writes each one the TRD does not yet state as one requirement of kind `reuse`. Empty for `update`.

changes.description: The changes to apply: for `complete`, the solutions architect's `trdChanges`; for `update`, what the TRD confirm step found does not resolve.

answerPath.description: The absolute path the answer is written to.

NoSource.description: An obligation the PRD implies for which neither the PRD nor the approved material gives a source.

prdRequirement.description: The PRD requirement heading that implies it.

why.description: What the architecture would have to state for the obligation to have a source.

TrdRequirement.description: One technical requirement as the TRD states it. The script records it in the matrix as one constraint that points at it (the Epic and this id, a heading of the TRD) with where it is stated and what it applies to; its statement stays in the TRD.

id.description: The requirement id, as the TRD gives it: the text of the requirement's own heading in the TRD.

statement.description: What must be true, with its checkable value.

appliesTo.description: The matrix id of the entry the requirement applies to; an empty string when it applies to the Epic as a whole.

TrdAnswer.description: trd-author's answer to one request. The TRD itself is the file at the request's `trdPath`.

requirementIds.description: The ids this write added, changed and removed.

removed.description: The ids of the requirements this write removed from the TRD.

requirements.description: Every requirement this answer's TRD write added or changed, exactly as the TRD now states it. A removed requirement is named in `requirementIds` only. The script records the matrix's constraints, each a pointer to its requirement, from these entries and from no other file.

WriteRequest.description: What the solutions architect decided for one group of arc42 sections, which architecture-maintainer writes into the architecture documents, arc42 and the detailed architecture; the script writes at most three, one per group.

facts.description: Each fact with its statement and reason, its one home and the documents that must link to it.

restatements.description: Each place that restates a fact and is to be replaced by a link to its home.

diagrams.description: Each diagram a diagram author returned, to place under its home.

resultPath.description: The absolute path the write result is written to.

entry.description: The id of the fact, or a description of the restatement, settlement or diagram.

WriteResult.description: architecture-maintainer's result for one write request.

headingsChanged.description: Each heading whose text was changed, as {source, heading}, including the heading of each folder index where a view was listed, moved or removed: an index edit is reported here like any other change, so it is promoted and committed with the views.

linksAdded.description: Each place a link to a home heading was added, as {source, heading}: the document the link was written in and the heading it sits under, never the link's target.

notApplied.description: Entries that could not be applied for any other reason.

RoutedItem.description: The lead's decision for one unsettled matter.

item.description: The id of the unsettled matter.

steps.description: The ids of the journal steps the lead added for it; empty for `reject`.

LeadRouting.description: architecture-team-lead's output: one decision for each item it was started for.

requirements.description: The business requirements or section 2 constraints in conflict.

matter.description: The id of the matter in the question file.

stands.description: The id of the position that stands; an empty string only when an owner concern is raised.

reason.description: Why that position stands, from the evidence the two sides gave.

losingPositionChanges.description: What the losing position must change.
